desc: Validate by brute force (exhaustive 3^M search on small random/adversarial cases) the conjecture: minimum cost is always in {1,2,3} or the goal is unachievable (-1); if refuted, find a counterexample and rethink.

Derive and verify exact O(M)-checkable conditions for K=1 (some I_i = [1,N]), K=2 (pair of sides from distinct ops covering [1,N]: interval+interval, interval+complement i.e. I_a ⊇ I_b with a≠b, complement+complement i.e. I_a ∩ I_b = ∅), K=3 (triples: 3 intervals; 2 intervals + 1 complement; 1 interval + 2 complements with distinct ops).
Implement final Python solution: fast input parsing via sys.stdin.buffer.read, O(N+M) memory, output K and the op list; verify against the four sample cases by reasoning.
Prove the K ≤ 3 theorem (if brute force supports it): any cover by interval/complement sides from distinct operations contains a sub-cover of size ≤ 3 from distinct operations.
Design O(M log M) or O(M) algorithms for each K check, including reconstruction of which operations/sides witness the cover (needed to output the op list).

Stress-test the current implementation against an exhaustive brute-force checker on small random/adversarial cases: generate many instances (N ≤ 8, M ≤ 6), run the CURRENT SOLUTION as a subprocess, simulate its printed ops to verify (a) final state is all ones, (b) printed K equals the true minimum from exhaustive 3^M search, and (c) -1 is printed exactly when unachievable; report any counterexample.

Run a larger stress test (2000+ trials) plus targeted worst-case inputs for the query_maxR O(M) fallback in the type-(iii) K=3 loop (e.g., many intervals sharing the same L and R so both top-2 prefix candidates are excluded for many b) to determine whether the O(M²) worst case is reachable; also do a performance sanity check at N=1e6, M=2e5 for TLE risk.

Fix any bugs found by the extended stress test; in particular audit the K=3 type (iii) per-b loop (query_maxR exclusion fallback correctness), the type (ii) top-2 candidate sufficiency under ties, and the K=3 type (iv) greedy chain distinctness; if the O(M²) fallback is reachable, replace query_maxR with a segment tree / sparse structure supporting max-R-with-exclusion queries in O(log M).
